title: WASP-39 b: Carbon Dioxide in a Puffy Hot Saturn
research_question: A low-density hot Saturn whose atmosphere became the first clear JWST exoplanet carbon-dioxide benchmark, paired here with a timing-adjusted TESS transit fit and a public NIRSpec spectrum.
datasets: TESS Sector 51 SPOC light curve (MAST, DOI 10.17909/t9-nmc8-f686)
NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars system parameters
public JWST NIRSpec PRISM transmission spectrum (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6959427)
principal_result: The repo's own TESS transit fit is strongly supported (ΔBIC = 12394.7, depth 23024.9 ± 219.7 ppm), and its own diagnostic on the public JWST spectrum finds a strong preference for the full ScCHIMERA model over a no-CO2 variant (Δχ² = 774.8) plus significant deviation from a flat spectrum (χ²/dof = 1089.6/93). The specific molecule detections and their sigma-significances (CO2 28.5σ, H2O 21.5σ, SO2 4.8σ) are cited from the peer-reviewed literature retrieval (Alderson et al. 2023), not computed by this repository.
headline_stat: ΔBIC = 12394.7 (TESS transit); Δχ² = 774.8 (full vs no-CO2 spectrum model, repository diagnostic)
evidence_status_note: the TESS transit and the JWST spectrum flatness/model-comparison tests are the repo's own reanalysis of public data; the molecule-level sigma values are literature citations layered on top.

title: WASP-17 b: Water Emission from an Inflated Hot Jupiter
research_question: An exceptionally inflated giant planet examined through a corrected TESS transit and three independent reductions of its JWST/NIRISS dayside emission spectrum.
datasets: TESS Sectors 12 & 38 SPOC light curves (MAST, DOI 10.17909/t9-nmc8-f686)
NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars system parameters
public JWST NIRISS/SOSS dayside emission spectrum, three independent reductions (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14003330)
methods: multi-sector ΔBIC and Cochran Q consistency check
weighted-flat spectrum fit across three reductions
principal_result: The TESS transit is strongly supported across two sectors (ΔBIC ≥ 10 in both; combined depth 16828.0 ± 89.3 ppm, Cochran Q p = 0.71). All three archived JWST NIRISS/SOSS reductions reject a flat, wavelength-independent dayside spectrum, which the repo treats as evidence of real spectral structure; the specific water-vapor attribution (H2O at 6.4σ) is drawn from the cited retrieval (Gressier et al. 2024), not computed here.
headline_stat: ΔBIC = 30092.5 (TESS transit, Sector 12); H2O reported at 6.4σ (literature)
evidence_status_note: repo performs its own transit fit and flat-spectrum statistical tests on public JWST reductions; the molecule-level significance is a literature citation.

title: WASP-18 b: An Ultra-Hot Jupiter in Water Emission
research_question: A massive, intensely irradiated giant on a 0.94-day orbit, combining a TESS transit fit with four reductions of a JWST dayside spectrum shaped by water emission.

public JWST NIRISS/SOSS dayside emission spectrum, four independent reductions (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7907569)

Four independent archived JWST reductions all show highly significant spectral structure (rejecting flat spectra), consistent with the cited water-emission detection (H2O >6σ, three emission features) and a combined 3.8σ optical-opacity signal attributed to H-/TiO/VO in Coulombe et al. 2023; those molecule-level significances are literature citations, not repo-computed retrievals.
headline_stat: ΔBIC = 454334.4 (TESS transit); H2O reported at >6σ (literature)
evidence_status_note: repo's own transit fit and multi-reduction flatness tests on public data; molecule attributions are literature citations.

NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars system parameters
public JWST MIRI/LRS phase-resolved emission spectrum, 14 wavelength bins x 4 orbital phases (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10525170)
methods: weighted-flat and linear-slope fits per orbital phase
principal_result: The TESS transit is strongly supported (ΔBIC = 104325.9, depth 26341.2 ± 110.6 ppm). The published retrieval (Bell et al. 2024) attributes this structure to water vapor at all phases and places a 2σ upper limit on methane (1-6 ppm); those molecule-level statements are literature citations, not repo-computed retrievals.
headline_stat: ΔBIC = 104325.9 (TESS transit); CH4 2σ upper limit 1-6 ppm (literature)
evidence_status_note: repo's own transit fit and phase-resolved flatness/slope tests on public MIRI data; molecule attribution and CH4 limit are literature citations.

title: TOI-836 b: What a Flat JWST Spectrum Can Rule Out
research_question: Does timing-adjusted TESS photometry confirm the TOI-836 b transit, and does the public JWST NIRSpec/G395H spectrum show resolved molecular features or instead statistically constrain what kind of atmosphere the planet cannot have?
datasets: NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
MAST TESS Sector 11 and Sector 38 SPOC light curves (DOI 10.17909/t9-nmc8-f686)
JWST NIRSpec/G395H published spectrum (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10658637, Alderson et al. 2024)
principal_result: TESS transit strongly supported (ΔBIC = 189.23, depth 605.9 ± 57.8 ppm, consistent across 2 supported sectors). The public JWST spectrum is statistically consistent with a flat line (chi-square/dof = 128.4/105, p = 0.0599) with no resolved H2O, CO2, CO, or CH4 feature; under a 0.1-bar opaque-pressure assumption this excludes clear H2-rich atmospheres below 250x solar metallicity and mean molecular weight below about 6 g/mol. Described in the README as 'a high-value null result.'
headline_stat: ΔBIC (null − transit) = 189.23; spectrum flatness chi-square/dof = 128.4/105 (p = 0.0599)

title: 55 Cancri e: Converting Season-Split Spitzer Occultation Depths into Dayside Temperatures
research_question: Do season-split Spitzer/IRAC occultation-depth measurements of lava world 55 Cancri e, independently inverted into dayside brightness temperatures via the Planck function, reproduce the season-to-season variability significance Demory et al. (2016) report?
datasets: NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
Demory et al. 2016 season-split Spitzer/IRAC 4.5-micron occultation depths (Table 4)
principal_result: The two season occultation depths (47 ± 21 ppm in 2012, 176 ± 28 ppm in 2013) differ at 3.7σ — matching the significance Demory et al. (2016) report from fitting all eight individual eclipses. This repo's own blackbody inversion gives 1639 K (2012) and 3330 K (2013), running above the paper's own MCMC-fit values of 1365 K and 2528 K; the gap is attributed to this script's simpler stellar-spectrum and planet-radius treatment, not a missing physical effect. The season-to-season swing itself holds up under both methods.
headline_stat: 3.7σ season-to-season occultation-depth difference (this repo's own inversion, matching Demory et al. 2016's significance)
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: GJ 1214 b: Inverting JWST MIRI Phase-Curve Photometry into Day/Night Brightness Temperatures
research_question: Does inverting real JWST MIRI phase-curve flux ratios of the flat-spectrum mini-Neptune GJ 1214 b into per-bin day and night brightness temperatures quantify genuine evidence for atmospheric heat redistribution, compared with Kempton et al. (2023)'s own published values?
datasets: NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
Kempton et al. 2023 MIRI phase-curve spectral fit results (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7703086)
principal_result: This repo's own per-bin weighted-mean brightness temperature is 575 ± 5 K dayside and 506 ± 9 K nightside, in the same range as (though not the same estimator as) Kempton et al.'s own joint-fit values of 553 ± 9 K and 437 ± 19 K. The day-night contrast is well below an ultra-hot Jupiter like WASP-121 b, broadly consistent with a real atmosphere redistributing heat imperfectly rather than a bare rock. Four of fourteen nightside bins are reported as unconstrained (0 K floor) rather than given a manufactured finite value.
headline_stat: 575 ± 5 K dayside / 506 ± 9 K nightside brightness temperature (this repo); cf. Kempton et al. 2023: 553 ± 9 K / 437 ± 19 K
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: HAT-P-11 b: An Independent In-Transit vs. Out-of-Transit Check on CARMENES Helium 10830 Å Data
research_question: Does this repo's own descriptive in-transit vs. out-of-transit flux statistic on Allart et al. (2018) CARMENES helium 10830 Å transit data support the published atmospheric-escape detection for the warm Neptune HAT-P-11 b, without conflating the two as the same measurement?

Allart et al. 2018 CARMENES helium transit data (Zenodo record 1473463)

headline_stat: 0.827% ± 0.064% in-transit helium flux dip, 12.9σ band S/N (this repo's estimator); paper's combined result 1.08% ± 0.05%
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: HD 189733 b: A Two-Window Band-Contrast Check on the JWST NIRCam Transmission Spectrum
research_question: Does a simple two-window band-contrast statistic run on the real JWST NIRCam transmission spectrum of HD 189733 b show significant structure consistent with, but not a substitute for, Fu et al. (2024)'s full-retrieval molecular detection significances?
datasets: NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
Fu et al. 2024 JWST NIRCam transmission spectrum, 139 bins, 2.4-5.0 microns (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11459715)
principal_result: Weighted mean transit depth 24183 ppm. This repo's own two-window comparison gives 239 ppm (22.1σ band S/N) for a CO2-adjacent window and 255 ppm (24.7σ band S/N) for an H2O/H2S-influenced window — high signal-to-noise structure, explicitly not molecule-specific detections. Fu et al. (2024)'s full atmospheric retrieval reports H2O at 13.4σ, CO2 at 11.2σ, CO at 5σ, and H2S at 4.5σ; both approaches agree the spectrum has real structure, but only the retrieval identifies which molecule causes it.
headline_stat: 22.1σ (CO2 window) / 24.7σ (H2O/H2S window) band S/N (this repo); Fu et al. 2024 retrieval: H2O 13.4σ, CO2 11.2σ, CO 5σ, H2S 4.5σ
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: HD 209458 b: A Four-Pipeline JWST MIRI Test for Magnesium Silicate Clouds
research_question: Using a 2026 JWST MIRI transmission spectrum, does the spread between four correlated data-reduction-tree leaves (testing for magnesium silicate clouds) exceed the photon-noise error on any single leaf's spectrum?
datasets: JWST MIRI LRS transmission spectrum (Chubb, Grant et al. 2026, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20089901)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
principal_result: Mean transit depth 14458 ppm across 28 wavelength bins (5.2-11.9 microns). The mean spread between the four reduction-tree leaves (122 ppm) is larger than the mean photon-noise error on any single leaf's spectrum (92 ppm) — a demonstration that data-reduction choices can matter as much as statistical noise for this kind of observation, matching the source paper's central point. The README explicitly notes this max-min spread is a sensitivity metric, not a formally calibrated systematic-uncertainty variance decomposition.
headline_stat: Mean transit depth 14458 ppm; inter-reduction spread 122 ppm vs. mean photon-noise error 92 ppm
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: K2-18 b: Testing the Contested CO2 Signal in a Combined, Offset-Corrected JWST Spectrum
research_question: Using a combined, offset-corrected JWST NIRISS SOSS + NIRSpec G395H + MIRI LRS spectrum, does the CO2 absorption band show a statistically significant excess over the nearby continuum, following up on the 2023 CO2/DMS claims and the ongoing debate over combining data from different JWST instruments?
datasets: Combined, offset-corrected JWST spectrum (2025 reanalysis, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16277833)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
methods: weighted mean and binning of native-resolution spectrum
principal_result: The CO2-band mean depth exceeds the nearby continuum by only ~4 ppm, at ~0.2 sigma — statistically indistinguishable from noise, and far from the confident detection the original 2023 NIRISS+NIRSpec-only analysis reported before the MIRI cross-check was available. The README is explicit this two-window comparison is a quick diagnostic, not a molecular retrieval. Independent retrieval-based work (Schmidt et al. 2025) points the same direction: methane confirmed at 4 sigma, with no significant evidence for CO2 or DMS in almost every data combination tested.
headline_stat: CO2-band excess ~4 ppm at ~0.2 sigma (statistically indistinguishable from noise); independent retrieval confirms CH4 at 4 sigma with no significant CO2/DMS evidence in almost every combination tested
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

research_question: Does the published JWST NIRSpec/G395H transmission spectrum of LHS 475 b statistically favor or rule out a flat (featureless) line, or specific candidate atmosphere models (pure methane, 1x-solar hydrogen-rich, clear Venus-like CO2, pure CO2)?
datasets: JWST NIRSpec/G395H spectrum (FIREFLy pipeline) and four published forward-model spectra (Lustig-Yaeger & Fu et al. 2023, Zenodo record 7925111)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
methods: reduced chi-squared and survival-function p-value model comparison (scipy.stats.chi2.sf)
principal_result: The spectrum is statistically indistinguishable from a flat line (chi-squared 50.70/55 dof, p=0.640). A primordial hydrogen-dominated envelope is decisively rejected (p<10^-300), and a cloudless pure-methane atmosphere is disfavored at high confidence (p=1.2e-7), while denser, higher-mean-molecular-weight options like a CO2-dominated, Venus-like atmosphere remain statistically consistent with the data (p=0.245 and 0.416) — matching the published conclusion that the data cannot yet distinguish a thick CO2 atmosphere, a thin Mars-like one, or bare rock.
headline_stat: Flat-line fit: chi-squared 50.70/55 dof, p=0.640; pure CH4 p=1.2e-7 (disfavored); H2-rich p<10^-300 (decisively disfavored); CO2 models p=0.245 and 0.416 (consistent)
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: TRAPPIST-1 e: A Flatness Test of the Decontaminated JWST NIRSpec/PRISM Spectrum
research_question: Is the decontaminated, stellar-contamination-corrected JWST NIRSpec/PRISM transmission spectrum (four combined transits) of TRAPPIST-1 e consistent with a flat, featureless spectrum, and how does that compare with the atmosphere constraints Espinoza et al. (2025) publish from their own retrieval?
datasets: Decontaminated NIRSpec/PRISM transmission spectrum (Espinoza et al. 2025, arXiv:2509.05414)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
principal_result: A chi-squared of 42.85 over 66 degrees of freedom (reduced chi-squared = 0.65, p = 0.988) across 67 wavelength points is consistent with a flat, featureless spectrum, matching the paper's own description. The README stresses flatness alone doesn't rule out an atmosphere. Espinoza et al. (2025), using their own retrieval framework, report ruling out cloud-free, hydrogen-dominated atmospheres (at least 80% H2 by volume) at better than 3 sigma, while denser secondary atmospheres remain possible.
headline_stat: Flat-line fit: chi-squared 42.85/66 dof, reduced chi-squared 0.65, p=0.988; H2-dominated atmospheres (>=80% H2) ruled out at >3 sigma by the source paper's own retrieval
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: WASP-96 b: JWST's First Published Exoplanet Spectrum and a Terminator Asymmetry Check
research_question: What do JWST's first published exoplanet transmission spectrum (NIRISS SOSS) and a later NIRSpec G395H morning/evening limb dataset show about WASP-96 b's water-vapor signature and possible terminator asymmetry?

NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
principal_result: NIRISS SOSS: 79 wavelength bins, weighted mean depth 14156 ppm, peak-to-trough amplitude 1267 ppm, with a clear water-band rise near 1.4 microns — the same feature announced in 2022. NIRSpec G395H: the evening-minus-morning terminator Rp/R* difference is consistent with zero at the precision achieved, matching the source study's own 'tentative' framing rather than a confident asymmetry detection.

title: WASP-107 b: A JWST NIRISS SOSS Transmission Spectrum of a Puffy Warm Neptune
research_question: What does a reduced JWST NIRISS SOSS transmission spectrum of the puffy, low-density warm Neptune WASP-107 b show, and how does it relate to separately reported SO2 and depleted-methane detections from other JWST instruments?
datasets: Reduced JWST NIRISS SOSS transit-depth spectrum, spectral orders 1 and 2 (Krishnamurthy et al., Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17085766)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars, queried live via TAP)
principal_result: 143 wavelength bins across 0.6-2.8 microns, weighted mean transit depth 2.062% +/- 0.0004%, with a rise toward the spectrum's blue and red edges consistent with water-vapor absorption. The SO2 and methane results discussed come from separate MIRI and NIRSpec observations not included in this NIRISS dataset, stated explicitly so the repo doesn't overclaim what one instrument's data shows on its own; a later NIRSpec study detected methane directly at 4.2 sigma, depleted roughly three orders of magnitude below equilibrium expectations.
headline_stat: Weighted mean transit depth 2.062% +/- 0.0004% across 143 bins; methane detected at 4.2 sigma (external NIRSpec study), depleted ~3 orders of magnitude below equilibrium

title: WASP-121 b: Day-Night Brightness Temperature Contrast from JWST Phase-Resolved Emission Spectroscopy
research_question: What is the day-night brightness-temperature contrast of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-121 b, extracted from JWST NIRSpec/G395H phase-resolved emission spectroscopy with each point's own posterior uncertainty propagated?
datasets: JWST NIRSpec/G395H phase-resolved emission spectrum, 349 wavelength channels x 36 orbital-phase bins (Evans-Soma, Sing et al. 2025, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20651891)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars)
methods: day/night phase-averaging with propagated posterior uncertainty
principal_result: Wavelength-averaged dayside brightness temperature 2751 +/- 3 K vs. nightside 1252 +/- 2 K — a day-night contrast of about 1493 +/- 4 K (range roughly 1235-1804 K across wavelength), pointing to very inefficient heat redistribution consistent with the extreme irradiation on the planet's 1.27-day orbit. The README notes this is a data comparison, not a model fit, and a separate bolometric analysis (Splinter et al. 2025) derives Tday=2717+/-17 K and Tnight=1562+/-19 K as the physically meaningful energy-budget numbers, which this repo's wavelength average is not intended to replace.
headline_stat: Day-night brightness-temperature contrast ~1493 +/- 4 K (dayside 2751+/-3 K, nightside 1252+/-2 K)

title: Box Least Squares Transit Detection: A From-Scratch Implementation Validated by Injection-Recovery
research_question: Can a from-scratch Box Least Squares (BLS) period search — blind over trial period, phase, and duration — recover a known synthetic transit signal injected into a simulated Kepler-noise-level light curve?
datasets: Synthetic light curve with injected transit signal, using Kepler's published ~100 ppm per-30-minute photometric noise level
NASA Exoplanet Archive (used only for a static geometric sanity-check calculation on HD 209458 b, not as input to the BLS search)
methods: Box Least Squares (BLS) period search (Kovacs, Zsom & Mazeh 2002)
principal_result: Recovered an injected synthetic transit signal with a blind period/phase/duration search: period 4.35 days recovered as 4.3500 days (0.00% error), duration 2.8 hours recovered as 3.13 hours (11.86% error, searched blind over 6 fractions), depth 850.0 ppm recovered as 833.8 ppm (1.90% error), with an in-transit depth signal-to-noise ratio of 77.8 sigma (uncorrected for search trials).
headline_stat: In-transit depth SNR 77.8 sigma; period recovered to 0.00% error, depth to 1.90% error

title: Keplerian Radial-Velocity Orbit Fitting: A From-Scratch Implementation Validated by Injection-Recovery
research_question: Can a from-scratch Keplerian RV model (with a Newton-Raphson Kepler-equation solver), fitted via a Lomb-Scargle periodogram and nonlinear least squares, recover a known orbit injected into a simulated dataset with HARPS-class noise and realistic irregular sampling?
datasets: Synthetic RV dataset (HARPS-class ~1 m/s photon noise plus ~1.5 m/s stellar jitter, irregular nightly cadence with seasonal gaps)
NASA Exoplanet Archive (sanity check against 51 Pegasi b's published orbital parameters)
principal_result: Recovered an injected Keplerian orbit from 60 irregularly sampled nights with HARPS-class noise: period 4.23 days recovered as 4.2303 days (0.01% error), semi-amplitude K 92.0 m/s recovered as 92.00 m/s (0.01% error), and minimum mass Mp sin i 235.7 Earth masses recovered as 235.8 Earth masses (0.00% error).
headline_stat: Period recovered to 0.01% error, K to 0.01% error, Mp sin i to 0.00% error

title: Point-Lens Microlensing: Blind Detection and Mass-Ratio Recovery of a Simulated Planetary Perturbation
research_question: Can a from-scratch point-source point-lens (PSPL) model plus planetary-perturbation scaling relations blindly detect and characterize a simulated planetary microlensing perturbation, without the detection or characterization steps ever referencing the injected signal's true parameters?
datasets: Simulated PSPL light curve sampled at KMTNet-class cadence (every 30 minutes) with ~2% ground-based crowded-field photometric noise
OGLE-2005-BLG-390Lb published parameters (sanity check, Beaulieu et al. 2006)
methods: planetary-perturbation amplitude/duration scaling relations (Mao & Paczynski 1991; Gould & Loeb 1992)
principal_result: The blind detection step found the injected perturbation window from residuals alone, landing within about half a day of the true injected center (recovered [21.48, 22.60] days vs. injected center at 22.0 days). The single-lens fit recovered the Einstein time (20.0 days injected vs. 20.010 days recovered, 0.05% error) and the mass ratio (1.50e-3 injected vs. 1.48e-3 recovered, 1.07% error), all without the search ever referencing the injected time or mass ratio.
headline_stat: Mass ratio recovered to 1.07% error; Einstein time recovered to 0.05% error
thumbnail_attribution: AI-generated artist's interpretation, not a direct image or observation.

title: Angular Differential Imaging: A From-Scratch ADI Pipeline Recovering a Companion Buried in Speckle Noise
research_question: Can a from-scratch Angular Differential Imaging (ADI) reduction pipeline recover a companion injected into a simulated speckle-limited imaging sequence, and what does a small-sample-corrected contrast curve say about the achievable detection limit?
datasets: Simulated 30-frame ADI sequence with a quasi-static speckle pattern and an injected companion at young-giant-planet-like contrast
HR 8799 b published parameters (sanity check, Marois et al. 2008)
methods: 5-sigma contrast curve with small-sample-statistics correction (Mawet et al. 2014)
principal_result: Recovered an injected companion at contrast 6.0e-4: the raw single-frame signal-to-noise was 0.64 sigma (not detectable), improving to 27.0 sigma after ADI reduction (a 42.2x SNR improvement, clear detection), recovering 88.3% of the injected flux, with a 5-sigma contrast limit of 1.5e-4 at the companion's separation (23 independent apertures).
headline_stat: ADI-reduced SNR 27.0 sigma (42.2x improvement over raw 0.64 sigma); 88.3% flux recovery; 5-sigma contrast limit 1.5e-4
